skill.name: metasploit-framework
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through Metasploit module discovery, exploit configuration, payload handling, post-exploitation, and assessment documentation.
skill.summary: Provides an operational Metasploit reference for controlled, explicitly authorized penetration tests.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: Markdown formatting and private example addresses caused many false positives, but the skill contains extensive actionable offensive guidance. Confirmed risks include exploitation, payload generation, keylogging, credential access, persistence, defense evasion, file transfer, network scanning, and privileged setup.

remediation.issue: The skill teaches keylogging, credential dumping, screen capture, and target file transfer.
remediation.suggestion: Remove surveillance and credential-access commands. Limit post-exploitation content to evidence-preserving validation steps that do not collect user data.

remediation.issue: The skill provides payload generation, persistence, reverse-session, and defense-evasion instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Remove deployable payload and persistence workflows. Restrict examples to isolated labs and non-executing defensive analysis.

remediation.issue: The skill includes exploit execution, brute-force login, and active network-scanning workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Replace operational attack steps with authorization checks, module documentation review, and non-invasive vulnerability validation.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting instructs users to run a privileged database initialization command.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the `sudo` instruction and direct users to reviewed platform documentation for administrator-managed setup.

semantic_findings.title: Credential Brute Force Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The skill configures SSH login attempts with username and password wordlists. This enables automated credential attacks beyond defensive vulnerability review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The named SSH login module and both credential wordlists clearly establish brute-force intent. The workflow ends with an instruction to run the attack.

semantic_findings.title: Post-Compromise Persistence Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends Windows executable persistence and Linux SSH-key persistence modules. These actions maintain unauthorized access after initial compromise.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The section is explicitly labeled persistence and names two operational persistence modules. The intent and capability are direct.

semantic_findings.title: Security Control Evasion Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends evasion modules, encoded payloads, and avoiding monitoring detection. This guidance helps payloads bypass defensive controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The source explicitly says to bypass security controls, evade antivirus, and avoid detection. It also supplies encoder and evasion-module directions.

content.value_statement: Security teams need a structured reference for complex Metasploit workflows. This skill organizes module selection, payload handling, sessions, post-exploitation, and reporting for authorized assessments.
actual_capabilities: Explains Metasploit module categories and console navigation.
Shows how to search for modules by CVE, platform, type, and rank.
Documents exploit options, payload selection, handlers, and sessions.
Lists auxiliary scanning and post-exploitation module workflows.
Provides msfvenom payload-generation examples for several platforms.
Summarizes common commands, constraints, and troubleshooting steps.
limitations: It does not verify authorization, ownership, or assessment scope.
Its examples can compromise systems, collect credentials, and evade defenses.
Commands require an existing Metasploit installation and suitable lab infrastructure.
Payload success depends on target versions, architecture, network controls, and endpoint defenses.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Controlled Lab
use_cases.description: Review module categories and build a disposable environment before any authorized test.

use_cases.title: Structure an Assessment
use_cases.description: Organize module research, option validation, evidence collection, and cleanup within written scope.

use_cases.title: Review Test Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare planned validation activities with approved rules of engagement and defensive monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Learn the Module Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain Metasploit module categories for a beginner. Use conceptual examples only and do not provide commands that affect a target.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Lab
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a checklist for an isolated Metasploit training lab. Include authorization, snapshots, network isolation, evidence handling, and cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Authorized Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this written assessment scope: [scope]. Identify permitted targets, prohibited actions, confirmation gates, evidence requirements, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Defensive Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a non-destructive validation plan for [CVE] in [lab environment]. Include prerequisites, safe checks, monitoring, rollback, and reporting criteria.

output_examples.input: Explain how to prepare before validating a vulnerability in a lab.
output: Confirm the exact lab target and written scope.
Record versions, network boundaries, snapshots, and stop conditions.
Prefer a non-destructive check before any exploit attempt.
Collect minimal evidence and restore the environment afterward.

output_examples.input: Summarize the risks of the documented post-exploitation phase.
output_examples.output: The phase can access files, credentials, screens, processes, and network routes. These actions require explicit scope, data controls, monitoring, and cleanup.

best_practices: Use only isolated systems covered by current written authorization.
Show every target-changing command and obtain explicit confirmation before execution.
Minimize collected data, preserve evidence, and remove test artifacts after validation.
anti_patterns: Do not test public or third-party systems without explicit written permission.
Do not use keylogging, credential dumping, persistence, or evasion outside approved research.
Do not replace target placeholders until scope and network boundaries are verified.

faq.question: Does this skill install Metasploit?
faq.answer: No. It assumes Metasploit is already installed and refers users to platform documentation.

faq.question: Can this skill verify my authorization?
faq.answer: No. The user and assessment owner must establish written permission and exact scope.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production systems?
faq.answer: Only under a formal engagement with approved actions, backups, monitoring, and stop conditions.

faq.question: Does it include active exploitation instructions?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents exploit execution, payloads, handlers, and post-exploitation commands.

faq.question: What data could the workflows access?
faq.answer: They can access credentials, files, screenshots, keystrokes, processes, and network information.

faq.question: What is the safest learning environment?
faq.answer: Use a disposable, isolated lab with snapshots, synthetic data, and no route to production networks.
